newsitem.title: FRANCE: French bank posts 20.9 pct rise in H1 profit.
newsitem.headline: French bank posts 20.9 pct rise in H1 profit.

text.p: Societe Generale, one of France's "Big Three" commercial banks, reported on Wednesday a 20.9 percent jump in first-half profits, helped by a sharp rise in revenues from financial market activities.

While not as staggering as the 80 percent climb in profits announced last week by Banque Nationale de Paris (BNP), the increase was a further indication the tide could be starting to turn for beleaguered French banks.

Net attributable profit for the first six months of the year rose to 2.73 billion francs from 2.26 billion on net banking income -- the banking equivalent of turnover -- that climbed 8.6 percent to 21.23 billion francs from 19.55 billion.
Gross operating profits rose to 6.17 billion francs from 5.49 billion while net new provisions were flat at 2.57 billion francs.

Profits from market activities and international operations soared 32.1 percent. This reflected a 43 percent rise in profits from market transactions, a 21.6 percent jump in profits from corporate finance activities and a 16.8 percent increase in profits from its overseas commercial network.
Profits from the bank's domestic activities rose 6.3 percent to three billion francs "despite a still difficult competitive environment."
The results were broadly in line with market expectations. The bank's shares closed unchanged at 590 francs.
But bank chairman Marc Vienot cautioned shareholders not to expect as big a profit jump in the second half, saying the first half was traditionally better for the bank.
"Do not multiply the first half results by two to get the full year. It's unlikely we will match in the second half the rise of the first half," Vienot said.
"But it's a year which has not started badly. The third quarter is in line, we are within our budget," he added. "It's not bad, there is no weakening."
Vienot said the bank would be stretched to make as many asset gains in the second half as it had done in the first.
He declined to say whether the bank was still interested in buying French bank CICfrom state-controlled insurer Groupe des Assurances Nationales.
While the bank had no strategic reason to expand, Vienot said it would "always look at a good banking network...which would not cost too much."
He stressed, however, that the bank would not jeopardise its profitability to grow.
